title: SSH tunnel
subtitle: Connect through an SSH server (bastion)
agentHelp: Uses the keys loaded in your SSH agent (ssh-agent, 1Password, the OpenSSH agent on Windows).
jumpHelp: Optional. SSH servers to go through first, in order and separated by commas. They use the same authentication.
trustedLegacy: (fingerprint from an older version, no server: no longer used)
trustedHelp: If a server changed its key, DBine refuses the connection. If the change is legitimate, forget that server, save and connect again: DBine will show you the new fingerprint to verify it.
tlsNote: Through a tunnel the database sees the connection coming from 127.0.0.1: if the server's TLS certificate doesn't cover it, turn on “Trust the server certificate”.
unknownBody: This is the first time DBine connects to {{host}}. Check that its key fingerprint matches the server's before you go on:

tabs.empty: This engine has no options here.

profiles.title: SSH profiles
profiles.intro: The SSH side of a tunnel (servers, user, authentication and verified keys) saved once and used by many connections. Each connection keeps its own database server; changes to a profile apply to its connections the next time they connect. Passwords and passphrases stay in the system keychain.
profiles.none: No SSH profiles yet. Create one here or save a connection's tunnel as a profile.
profiles.name: Profile name
profiles.dialogHelp: Connections that use this profile take the SSH server, user and authentication from here; the database server is still each connection's own.
profiles.removeConfirm: Delete the SSH profile “{{name}}”? No connection uses it.
profiles.removeInUse_one: The SSH profile “{{name}}” is used by 1 connection:
profiles.removeInUse_other: The SSH profile “{{name}}” is used by {{count}} connections:
profiles.removeInUseAfter: If you delete it, each of them keeps a copy of its SSH settings (secrets included) as its own settings, so they keep connecting as before.
profiles.ownHelp: Save them as a profile to use them in other connections; saved secrets move to the profile without leaving the keychain.
profiles.usingHelp: The profile gives the SSH server, user and authentication; the database server is this connection's. Changes to the profile apply the next time it connects.
profiles.missing: The chosen SSH profile no longer exists: pick another one or go back to this connection's own settings.
